title: Aurumix AURX: Secondary Market Liquidity Audit
subtitle: How deep a stablecoin pool AURX needs, what trades will cost in it, and how much of it is gold.
tagline: Built by founders. Designed for founders.
legal: Prepared by Tokenomics.net for Aurumix. © 2026. Confidential.

intro: AURX can trade on a secondary market, and the Mechanism Design Document already says not to seed a thin pool at launch. This audit sizes a pool that is not thin: one where everyday amounts trade at almost exactly the gold price and the largest bar can still exit inside the entry fee. It covers liquidity only, because AURX has no allocations, investors or unlocks to audit.

stats.label: Recommended pool: USD 449k stablecoin plus 2.97 kg of gold
Depth of a ±10% concentrated pool against a simple pool, same capital
What a simple (V2) pool would need for the same service

findings.title: A simple pool does not work for AURX
findings.body: A V2 pool spreads its capital across every price, most of which gold will never reach. At USD 1m it takes only USD 1,765 of selling inside 1%, and a 100 g holder moves its price about 5.7%. Holding the service standard would need USD 12.1m.

findings.title: A concentrated pool does, for under a million
findings.body: Two thirds of the capital in a ±10% band around the gold price: USD 870k meets the standard. A USD 2,000 trade costs 0.37%, a 100 g exit 0.76%, and a 1 kg exit stays inside the 5% entry fee. A ±5% band does the same with USD 445k.

findings.title: The band needs an owner
findings.body: Gold leaves a ±5% band within a month in two runs out of five, and a ±10% band in 3%. Once outside, capacity falls 40 to 85 times and the pool shows the discount the design forbids. ±10% needs a quarterly review; ±5% needs a market maker.

findings.title: The pool undercuts the entry fee
findings.body: A buyer who can reach the pool pays about 0.3 to 0.8% over gold instead of 5%. That is fine if it is a deliberate choice for existing holders and crypto-native buyers. Whether Aurumix may provide the liquidity itself is a question for counsel.
